title: ODF-T FY26 Bledsoe Ferry Rehabilitation Project
description: Presolicitation Notice: Synopsis for Commercial Construction Services (Prepared in accordance with RFO Subpart 5.1 and RFO Subpart 12.1) This presolicitation notice is prepared in accordance with the requirements outlined in RFO 5.101, supplemented with additional information provided in this notice. This announcement serves as the public presolicitation notice for this acquisition. A formal written solicitation will not be posted to the System for Award Management (SAM.gov); instead, the Government will solicit quotations directly from suppliers. Solicitation Information The anticipated solicitation number for this acquisition is W912DQ26QA081 for the FY26 Bledsoe Ferry Rehabilitation Project at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Project Office at Harry S Truman Lake (Warsaw, MO). IAW RFO 12.201-1(c)(2) - Simplified Procedures Method To promote maximum competition and streamline acquisition, the Contracting Officer has chosen to solicit quotations directly from suppliers for this acquisition. When soliciting directly, the following conditions apply: A presolicitation notice must be posted in the Governmentwide Point of Entry (GPE) per RFO FAR 5.101(a). Quotations must be solicited from a minimum of three sources [RFO 12.201-1(c)(2)(ii)]. Whenever practicable, solicitations should include at least two sources not previously contacted [RFO 12.201-1(c)(2)(iii)]. No formal solicitation document will be posted on SAM.gov. For inquiries, please contact Mr. Cade Zelinsky at cade.s.zelinsky@usace.army.mil or call 816-389-3143. The incorporated provisions and clauses are in effect through the current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC) and the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). (1) Point of Contact [RFO 5.101(c)(1)] Contract Specialist Cade Zelinsky (816) 389-3143 cade.s.zelinsky@usace.army.mil Contracting Officer Christopher W. Anderson (816) 389- 3850 christopher.w.anderson@usace.army.mil (2) Set-aside [RFO 5.101(c)(2) & RFO 6.102-2] Total Small Business Set-Aside (100%) (3) Codes for Services or Supplies [RFO 5.101(c)(3)] a. Product Service Code (PSC): Y1JZ - Construction of Miscellaneous Buildings b. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS): 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (4) Description of Services and Award Procedures [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(i) & (ii)] The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Kansas City District has a requirement for a construction contract for the FY26 Bledsoe Ferry Rehabilitation Project at the Harry S Truman Lake Project in Warsaw, MO. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, and materials required for the project. The primary scope includes the rehabilitation of the existing sewer lift station utilizing 100% Solids Epoxy lining; the complete demolition, removal, and disposal of the existing comfort station; site preparation and earthwork to facilitate the placement, anchoring, and utility installation of a new pre-constructed concrete comfort station and concrete sidewalks; and the replacement of the primary electrical service pole, drop, and associated wiring infrastructure. This requirement will be procured using the simplified procedures outlined in RFO 12.201-1, used in conjunction with RFO Part 36 for construction. The Government intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The anticipated contract award date is 31 October 2026 (5) Technical Data Access [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(iv)] The complete Statement of Work (SOW), detailing exact specifications, testing parameters, and safety requirements, will be provided directly to the solicited vendors. Other interested vendors may request the SOW from the Contract Specialist listed above. (6) Equitable Adjustments for Change Orders [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(v), RFO 36.101-4, & DFARS PGI 205.103-70] Information regarding USACE policies on definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found at: https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/. In accordance with DFARS PGI 205.103-70(b), no data is available regarding the timely definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts. (7) Universal Submission Statement [RFO 5.101(c)(4)(vi)] All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. (8) Applicable FAR Clauses [RFO 12.205 & RFO 36.101-7]: The solicitation and the resulting award incorporate one or more provisions and clauses by reference, carrying the same legal force as if provided in full text. The Contracting Officer will provide full versions upon request. Contractors are advised that certain provisions include data blocks that must be completed and submitted with the quotation. Instead of submitting the full text of these provisions, you may identify them by paragraph identifier and provide the required information. Full text is also available electronically at the following addresses: Federal Acquisition Regulations System (FAR) https://www.acquisition.gov/far Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement https://www.acquisition.gov/dfars **Applicable FAR Clauses: ** - FAR 52.212-1: Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-2: Evaluation - Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-4: Contract Terms and Conditions - Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.236-5: Material and Workmanship - FAR 52.236-7: Permits and Responsibilities Important SAM Registration Notice: In accordance with FAR provision 52.204-7, incorporated by reference in this solicitation, the prospective awardee must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at https://sam.gov to be eligible for award. Find your local APEX Accelerators to get free help completing registration in SAM.gov. Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: Title: Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program Multi-Mission Dry Dock, Multiple Award Construction Contract Type: Pre-Solicitation Notice Location: Primarily at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF), located at Naval Base Kitsap (NBK) Bremerton, Washington and other areas under the cognizance of Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Pacific. Solicitation Method: NAVFAC intends to issue one (1) solicitation in September 2026 that results in the award of approximately five (5) Indefinite-Delivery Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACC) primarily in support of the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program (SIOP) Multi-Mission Dry Dock. Solicitation and award of the MACC is anticipated to utilize single phase (one-step) Design-Build (DB) selection procedures. Anticipated Evaluation Factors: Anticipated non-cost/price and price evaluation factors for the solicitation are summarized as follows: Factor 1 � Technical Approach (acceptable/unacceptable) Factor 2 � Experience Factor 3 � Past Performance Factor 4 � Small Business Utilization and Participation Factor 5 � Safety (acceptable/unacceptable) Price NOTE: The Government anticipates that evaluation of Factor 2 � Experience will encompass relevant projects for BOTH construction projects AND design projects. Period of Performance/Maximum Value: The period of performance is anticipated to be a base period of 5-years and one (1) 5-year option period for a maximum possible duration of 10-years; or an aggregate maximum estimated value of $15,000,000,000 for all task orders, whichever occurs first. NAICS Codes: This MACC will encompass a wide range of DB and Design-Bid-Build (DBB) type projects primarily representative of North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) codes 237990 (primary) Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction as well as 236220 (secondary) Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. Task Order Range: The typical size of major construction task orders will range from $2,000,000,000 to $6,000,000,000; however, smaller task orders may be issued to support smaller efforts such as Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) and/or Alternative Technical Concepts (ATC). Task orders may be above this limit; however, contractors are not obligated to accept such task orders under the general terms of the contract. For evaluation purposes, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that construction projects with a minimum value of $500,000,000 will be deemed relevant. The Navy anticipates that most work under the MACC will be initiated by task order(s) that are competed amongst all the MACC holders (firms awarded one of the potential contracts). Additionally, all MACC holders may be issued task orders for the same scope of work for ECI and/or ATC or where justified, task order awards may be issued to a single MACC holder. The Navy makes no representation as to the number of task orders or actual amount of work to be ordered; however, each MACC holder is anticipated to receive a minimum guarantee in the amount of $1,000,000. As subsequent task orders are awarded which exceed the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee, the $1,000,000 minimum guarantee will be de-obligated and the Government�s obligation for the minimum guarantee for the contract will be satisfied. Bonding Capacity: To qualify for this MACC, the Government anticipates that the solicitation may stipulate that Offerors will need to demonstrate single project bonding capacity of $1,000,000,000 and an aggregate bonding capacity of $3,000,000,000. Acquisition Timeline (Anticipated): Industry Day: 20 August 2026 (actual) Issue MACC Solicitation: 30 September 2026 MACC Pre-Proposal Conference: October 2026 MACC Proposals Due: December 2026 MACC Award: June 2027 Issue Alternative Technical Concept (ATC) Task Order(s): June 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Initial): August 2027 ATC Proposals Due (Final): November 2027 RFP Task Order Marine Package #1: November-December 2027 Planned task order award of Marine Package #1: June 2028 Purpose and Scope: The focus of this MACC will be the construction of a new proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock in support of SIOP requirements at PSNS & IMF, located at NBK Bremerton, Washington. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock preferred location is within the existing Dry Dock 3 footprint, existing Pier 6, and existing Pier 7; and will include dry dock drainage, dewatering, and flooding systems; a caisson; roadways and rail networks; portal crane track; access and egress elements; mechanical, electrical, and communications systems; support buildings; and utility routing tunnels. The proposed project also includes demolition of facilities and utilities. The Multi-Mission Dry Dock is a fully pressure-relieved dry dock capable of accommodating shipyard repair services for the newest Ford-class aircraft carrier, Nimitz-class carriers, and other surface and subsurface ships served by PSNS & IMF. Dredging south of Multi-Mission Dry Dock is proposed for the Double-Wall Cofferdams, which provides means to support construction of Multi-Mission Dry Dock in the dry, and provides hydraulic cutoff in the permanent condition. The bathymetry in Sinclair Inlet provides adequate water depths to support the drafts of the respective design vessels at berth and during docking/undocking evolutions. Site access is anticipated to be a combination of a temporary fixed pier southeast of existing Building 460, a contractor access road at Bremerton Gate, existing Piers 6 & 7, Dry Dock 3, and the South Gate vehicle inspection building. Prior to establishing the above-described entry points the Navy requires the contractor to install a temporary Controlled Industrial Area (CIA) fence that will encompass the project site. For more information on the proposed Multi-Mission Dry Dock project see: https://bremertonwaterfrontimprovementseis.com/ https://multimissiondrydock.com/ Potential Risk Mitigations: The Navy is considering the following risk mitigation measures including but not limited to: Early Contractor Involvement (ECI) Economic Price Adjustment (EPA) Award Fee and/or Schedule Incentive Reduced small business subcontracting targets One or more of the items under this acquisition may be subject to Free Trade Agreements or the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement. Large Business Offerors will be required to submit an acceptable small business subcontracting plan. Competition Description: A sources sought notice for this procurement was posted on 29 June 2026 on SAM.gov to conduct market research of interested sources. The market research included an assessment of relevant qualifications and capabilities of potentially qualified firms. As a result of the market research analysis, a determination was made to solicit this procurement on an unrestricted basis inviting full and open competition. THIS SOLICITATION WILL BE OFFERED IN ELECTRONIC FORMAT ONLY. NO HARD COPIES WILL BE PROVIDED. The solicitation will be available on the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module at https://piee.eb.mil/. Amendments will be posted on the PIEE website. This will be the only method of amendment distribution; therefore, it is the OFFERORS� RESPONSIBILITY TO CHECK THE WEBSITE PERIODICALLY FOR ANY AMENDMENTS TO THE SOLICITATION. Prospective Offerors MUST register on the PIEE website. Training and instructions on how to submit proposals are available at https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/index.xhtml. Offerors must also be properly registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) system at https://sam.gov/ in order to participate in this procurement.

title: Criminal History Record Information (CHRI) Access
description: The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), Personnel Vetting (PV), Data Collection and Analysis (DC&A), has a requirement to obtain access to international criminal, law enforcement, and public safety records over a secure network. The secure network must provide access to Criminal History Record Information (CHRI) repositories for multiple law enforcement agencies to include United States local areas, regional areas, States and Territories, Washington D.C., Canada, and if possible, any other relevant area where CHRI searches may need to be conducted. Criminal, law enforcement, and public safety records must be provided in accordance with Federal Investigative Standards (FIS) and 5 U.S. Code � 9101- Access to criminal history records for national security and other purposes. This information is vital to the mission of DCSA in the performance of personnel vetting and conducting background investigations (BI) for the departments and agencies of the Federal Government. BIs are required to determine an individual�s eligibility for access to classified information, assignment to or retention in positions with sensitive duties, or other designated duties requiring such investigations as defined by FIS and Trusted Workforce (TW) 2.0 requirements. Additionally, DC&A has a continuing need for this information in support of TW 2.0 continuous vetting requirements.

description: Przedmiot zamówienia obejmuje usługę kompleksowego utrzymania czystości w obiekcie Śląskiego Oddziału Regionalnego i obiektach 17 Biur Powiatowych Agencji Restrukturyzacji i Modernizacji Rolnictwa wraz z usługami utrzymania terenów zewnętrznych. Usługi w szczególności obejmują: mycie i dezynfekcję biurek, odkurzanie wykładzin oraz mycie powierzchni płaskich, mycie i dezynfekcję klamek, poręczy oraz wszystkich pozostałych stref dotykowych, opróżnianie koszy na śmieci oraz pojemników w niszczarkach biurowych w momencie ich zapełnienia wraz z wymianą wkładów foliowych i każdorazowe wynoszenie (nieczystości, ścinek) w odpowiednie miejsce zgodnie z systemem zbierania i segregowania odpadów obowiązującym w obiekcie oraz aktualnymi przepisami w tym zakresie, mycie płaskich powierzchni podłóg oraz powierzchni podestów i schodów w ramach ciągów komunikacyjnych (jeśli takie występują) środkami do tego przeznaczonymi, sprzątanie schodów i wejść (podestów) do budynków tj.; w okresie wiosenno-letnim: zamiatanie schodów, odkurzanie wycieraczek, w okresie jesienno-zimowym: usuwanie błota pośniegowego, zwalczanie śliskości i oblodzeń, odśnieżanie i posypywanie środkami uszorstniającymi wraz z zapewnieniem odpowiednich do takich czynności środków, przy czym odśnieżanie i posypywanie terenów utwardzonych winno być wykonane do godz. 7:00 oraz sukcesywnie w ciągu dnia w przypadku opadów śniegu, dbanie o czystość wraz z dezynfekcją urządzeń sanitarnych: umywalki (zlewozmywaki), sedesy, pisuary, bidety, podajniki na mydło w płynie oraz ręczniki papierowe typu ZZ, blaty i stoliki kuchenne środkami do tego przeznaczonymi, usuwanie plam z wykładzin i mebli tapicerowanych w momencie powstania i zlecenia ich usunięcia przez Zamawiającego, usuwanie śladów rąk i innych zabrudzeń z powierzchni drzwi, mebli i powierzchni szklanych oraz inne pozostałe czynności wymienione w Załączniku nr 1 do SWZ - Opis przedmiotu zamówienia. Częstotliwość wykonywania poszczególnych usług oraz zastosowanie niezbędnych środków higienicznych została dokładnie określona w załączniku nr 1 do SWZ - Opis przedmiotu zamówienia. 1.Wykonawca zobowiązany będzie do realizowania usług będących przedmiotem Umowy zgodnie z zachowaniem następujących zasad: a) Realizacje czynności składających się na kompleksowe utrzymanie czystości wewnątrz obiektów i utrzymanie terenów zewnętrznych będą realizowane od poniedziałku do piątku w dni robocze w godzinach pracy ARiMR tj. od 7:30 – 15:30 za wyjątkiem czynności związanych z odśnieżaniem oraz posypywaniem materiałem ciernym terenów zewnętrznych i odśnieżaniem budynków (sople, nawisy śnieżne, itp.), a w okresie wzmożonych opadów śniegu na bieżąco, które powinny być wykonane również poza godzinami otwarcia jednostek ARiMR, tak by teren był przygotowany do użytkowania o godzinie 7:00 rano. b) Sprzątanie obiektów powinno być zorganizowane w taki sposób, aby nie zakłócać pracy Oddziału Regionalnego/Biura Powiatowego. c) Dla każdego sprzątanego lokalu osoby sprzątające powinny posiadać na wyposażeniu podest typu schodki lub drabinkę umożliwiający wyjście na wysokość co najmniej 1 m. d) Wykonawca w trakcie realizacji Umowy zobowiązany jest do przestrzegania zasad w zakresie bezpieczeństwa informacji i bezpieczeństwa fizycznego, przepisów dot. ochrony danych osobowych, przepisów PPOŻ., BHP, sanitarnych, ochrony środowiska oraz bezpieczeństwa osób i mienia. Do wykonania prac na wysokości powyżej 1m Wykonawca zobowiązany jest skierować osoby posiadające odpowiednie uprawnienia i badania lekarskie oraz wyposażone w środki techniczne i środki ochrony osobistej niezbędne do bezpiecznego i należytego wykonania usług sprzątania. e) Detergenty, środki dezynfekujące, środki czystości i środki toaletowe powinny posiadać karty charakterystyki lub inne prawnie obowiązujące dokumenty potwierdzające dopuszczenie ich do obrotu i stosowania. Zamawiający nie dopuszcza do realizacji umowy preparatów rejestrowanych jako kosmetyki ( mydło w płynie ). Usługa winna być wykonana zgodnie z przepisami sanitarnymi tak, aby użyte w celach czyszczących substancje i preparaty nie stanowiły zagrożenia dla zdrowia, życia człowieka i środowiska tzn. w szczególności odpowiadające wymogom aktualnej ustawy z dnia 25 lutego 2011 r. o substancjach chemicznych i ich mieszaninach – wszystkie dostarczane i używane środki sanitarne, higieniczne i chemiczne muszą być opatrzone łatwo dostępnymi etykietami, zawierającymi dane dotyczące składu/ atestu, gramatury itp.; pojemniki ze środkami higienicznymi/ czyszczącymi powinny być oryginalnie zapakowane, nie dopuszcza się możliwości przelewania, przekładania ich do innych opakowań, bez oznaczeń producenta, pod rygorem naliczenia kar przewidzianych w Umowie. f) Na żądanie Zamawiającego Wykonawca udzieli informacji o jakości stosowanych narzędzi, materiałów, środków czystości, detergentów, materiałów uszorstniających itp.

title: Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility and Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition, HIANG, JBPHH, HI
description: 07-Oct-2026: Posting Amendment 0001, preproposal conference slides and sign-in attendance sheet in PIEE/Solicitation Module. The purpose of Amendment 0001 is to change Questions due NLT 16 Oct 2026, 5:00 PM HST, and the offer due date to 30 Oct 2026, 3:30 PM HST. ____23-Sep-2026: This is a Solicitation Notice, Request for Proposal. Single Project RFP Set-Aside for Small Businesses NAICS Code: 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Hawaii National Guard intends to issue a Request for Proposals (RFP) to award a single firm fixed-price contract for services, non-personal, to provide all plant, labor, transportation, materials, tools, equipment, appliances and supervision necessary for the Construction of KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility and KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition located on the Hawaii Air National Guard campus, at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii. These projects will be concurrent. KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility - Construct a new Munitions Maintenance and Inspections facility by utilizing conventional design and construction methods to accommodate the facility mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 2,400 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Micro-pile Foundations: Specialized foundation engineering featuring micro-piles to mitigate challenging soil conditions and ensure seismic structural integrity. Cast-in-Place Concrete: Constructing robust concrete slab-on-grade, concrete walls, capping beams, and associated structural masonry elements. Structural Framing and Enclosure: Utilizing cold-formed metal framing, insulated metal wall panels, and structural steel support systems. Roofing: Installation of high-performance standing seam metal roofing, complete with prefinished gutters, downspouts, and weather barrier wraps. Specialized Systems: Installation of mechanical HVAC systems (including specialized 20-ton air conditioning systems), interior plumbing, lightning/grounding protection, and communication infrastructure. Fire Protection: A complete fire alarm-mass notification system and wet-pipe sprinkler suppression system. In addition to the base work described above, the solicitation will include the following option line items: 1. MAC Pad - Construct 1,167 SY concrete pad for the Material Assembly Center (MAC), required for constructing munitions, along with new asphalt pavement for access and egress to the facility maintenance bays. KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition - Construct an addition to the Munitions Cube Storage Facility (B3552) utilizing conventional design and construction methods to support the F-22 mission. This project has a statutory cost limitation $14M for Unspecified Minor Military Construction (UMMC) Project - Adjustment of Dollar Limitations for Location pursuant to 10 USC Section 2805. Project square footage is estimated at 1,320 SF. Work covered in this project includes but is not limited to: Substructure and Enclosure: Micro-pile foundations, concrete wall structures, cast-in-place concrete slabs, and 12 in. thick concrete walls designed for high-hazard storage specifications. Framing and Roofing: Structural steel framing, roof joists, and standing seam metal roofing matching existing facility standards. Exterior Elements: Erection of new asphalt pavement adjacent to the existing facility access to provide adequate logistics and material handling access around the new facility addition. Specialized Protection: Maintenance facility lightning and grounding protection systems, along with integrated fire detection and alarm reporting systems connected back to the base reporting system. APPLICABLE TO BOTH PROJECTS: RAB Lighting exterior wall packs and area lights are sole source/brand name specific for compatibility with existing installation systems (noted justifications will be included with solicitation). Project Phasing and Security Gates: The contractor will be required to erect a temporary security fence around the construction zone in accordance with the project staging and phasing drawings. Escort Requirements: Escort personnel shall be required when erecting the temporary security fence, performing work occurring outside the temporary security fence, and connecting utilities to the existing system. Secured Zone Access: Once the temporary security fencing is approved and accepted by the Contracting Officers Representative (COR), no escort shall be required within the active secured work zone during construction, allowing the contractor to work within the secured boundary unimpeded. The magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000 total. KNMD209085 Munitions Maintenance and Inspection Facility project duration will be 733 calendar days after notice to proceed to include inspection and punch list. KNMD209086 Conventional Munitions Cube Storage Addition project duration will be 456 calendar days after notice to proceed to include inspection and punch list. This action is being solicited as a set-aside 100% for Small Businesses. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236220, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. title: Garden Maintenance Services
description: The U.S. Embassy in Lusaka, Zambia, intends to issue Request for Quotations (RFQ) No. 19ZA6027Q0001 for Garden Maintenance Services. The Embassy plans to award a firm-fixed-price contract with an indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) component for temporary additional services. The contract will have one base year and four option years. Scope of Work. The contractor will provide all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision for full gardening and grounds maintenance at U.S. Government-owned or -managed properties in Lusaka. Services include, but are not limited to: Lawn care: grass cutting, edging, trimming, weeding, and turf repair Pruning of trees, shrubs, and hedges Leaf and debris removal Watering Pest and disease control Upkeep of all designated green spaces The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The Government may award the contract based on the initial offer without discussion. The resultant contract will be a firm fixed price type contract. Obtaining the Solicitation. The Embassy will post the RFQ on [SAM.gov / Embassy Lusaka website] . Offerors are responsible for checking for amendments. Quotations must be in English and submitted electronically to Lusaka-procurement@state.gov in MS Word, MS Excel, or PDF format. Each email must be under 30 MB.

title: FTA Broad Agency Announcement (FY26) -- �Research Initiatives in Support of Safety, Accessibility, and Mobility in Public Transportation
description: AMENDMENT No. 0001 - The purpose of this amendment is to extend the due date to October 30, 2026. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) from the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) solicits applied research projects to improve the safety, reliability, efficiency, and accessibility of public transportation in the United States. Purpose: To solicit innovative applied research that reduces deployment risks, improves safety, lowers costs, and facilitates domestic transit manufacturing. Eligibility: This is an unrestricted solicitation; any responsible source (excluding Federal Government-owned businesses) may submit a concept paper. Teaming and collaboration are encouraged. Funding: Individual awards typically range between $150,000 and $500,000, subject to fund availability. While cost sharing is not always mandatory, projects including transit operator partnerships and cost sharing are preferred. Technology Readiness: Projects should focus on technology readiness levels (TRL) 3 through 6, with a preference for proof-of-concept testing (TRL 3).

title: Request for Information (RFI): Identifying the Next Generation of NSF X-Labs Topics
description: The U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP), is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to obtain public input on scientific and technological opportunities that could become future topics for the NSF X-Labs Initiative. NSF seeks information on high impact platform technology opportunities, critical technical bottlenecks, enabling infrastructure, potential partnerships, and conditions under which dedicated X-Labs teams could accelerate scientific and technological breakthroughs. This RFI is for planning and information gathering purposes only. It is not a solicitation, funding opportunity, or request for proposals, and NSF will not make an award based on responses to this RFI. Responses are due October 30, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

description: CALL FOR SOLUTIONS. This Call for Solutions is the first call under the DRAFT CSO � U.S. Army Aviation Training, formerly �DRAFT CSO � Flight School Next�, W9113M-25-S-C006. This requirement is the future of the Initial Entry Rotary Wing (IERW) Training Program at Fort Rucker, Alabama, known as Flight School Next (FSN). The contractor shall provide all services and equipment required to train pilots to a U.S. Army standard equivalent to the Federal Aviation Administration�s (FAA) commercial helicopter pilot certification, including single engine aircraft, parts, maintenance, instructors (both academic and flight), and simulation (if required). The place of performance to train the rotary wing pilots will be located at Fort Rucker, Alabama. The intent of the FSN Program is to increase the proficiency of U.S. Army aviators using commercially available equipment and instruction practices.

Fiber Dial Room Refurbishment
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA) Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors to provide refurbishment services for the Fiber Dial Room and implement point-to-point fiber connectivity upgrades. This initiative supports BEA�s commitment to maintaining robust and reliable communications infrastructure across INL facilities. BACKGROUND The Fiber Dial Room requires refurbishment and modernization to support enhanced fiber optic connectivity and point-to-point communication capabilities. The scope of work may include the following: Refurbishment of the Fiber Dial Room, including structural and environmental improvements. Installation and configuration of point-to-point fiber connections. Integration with existing network infrastructure and systems. Compliance with DOE cybersecurity, safety, and operational standards. Testing and documentation to ensure full functionality and reliability. INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL is operated under a management and operating contract with the Department of Energy and as such, the Davis-Bacon Act applies for contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of buildings or works at INL. Construction work at the laboratory Site covered under the Davis-Bacon Act is additionally subject to the INL Site Stabilization Agreement (SSA). These Site areas include all areas within the 890-square mile boundary, including the Material and Fuels Complex, Central Facilities Area, Advanced Test Reactor, Radioactive Waste Management Complex, and Specific Manufacturing Capability. The agreement is between signatory contractors and labor unions performing such work. Information regarding the INL Site Stabilization Agreement is available from the Site Labor Coordinator at (208) 524-4404 or at lance@sitelabor.org. Construction work performed at Idaho Falls facilities is not subject to these agreements. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Germany – Pumps – Los 2.4 Lieferung Pumpen Wärmespeicher
description: Im Rahmen des Projekts „Errichtung Großwärmespeicher und dessen hydraulische Einbindung in die Fernwärmeverteilung am Standort HKW West“ (Gesamtprojekt WSPW) der Stadtwerke Karlsruhe soll ein Wärmespeicher zur Sicherstellung einer nachhaltigen, zukunftsfähigen und gesicherten Wärmeversorgung realisiert werden. Die verfahrenstechnische Aufgabe des zu planenden 2-Zonen-Wärmespeichers soll in der Speicherung und bedarfsgerechten Bereitstellung thermischer Energie innerhalb des Fernwärmesystems bestehen. Der drucklos ausgeführte Wärmespeicher soll durch die Ausbildung einer thermischen Schichtung die getrennte Aufnahme und Abgabe von Wärme auf unterschiedlichen Temperaturniveaus ermöglichen. Durch die hydraulisch entkoppelte Einbindung in das Fernwärmenetz über ein separates Vor- und Rücklaufsystem soll der Wärmespeicher zum Ausgleich von Lastschwankungen sowie zur zeitlichen Entkopplung von Wärmeerzeugung und -verbrauch beitragen. Bei diesem Beschaffungsvorhaben sollen funktionstüchtige Vor- und Rücklauf- sowie Beimischpumpen einschließlich aller zum bestimmungsgemäßen Betrieb erforderlichen Komponenten innerhalb der spezifizierten Liefergrenzen geplant, hergestellt und geliefert werden.

title: Ireland – Construction work for electricity power lines – The MaresConnect 750MW HVDC Interconnector System
description: The MaresConnect Project is a proposed 750 MW, 320 kV High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) electricity interconnector linking Denbighshire, Wales and North County Dublin, Ireland. Developed by MaresConnect Limited, a joint venture between Foresight Group Holdings Ltd and Etchea Energy Nominees Ltd, the project will transmit electricity via approximately 240 km of subsea and underground cables between new converter stations on each side. It aims to enhance security of supply, market integration, and renewable energy utilisation between the Irish and GB grids. MaresConnect shall utilise Voltage Source Converter (VSC) technology and the configuration shall be a Symmetrical Monopole. The rated DC voltage shall be +/-320 kV. The link shall be bi-directional and shall have a rated power (receiving end) of 750 MW. The project is being procured as separate EPC (Turnkey) contracts, divided into four lots: LOT 1A: EPC for two HVDC Converter Stations; LOT 1B: EPC for one Irish 400kV AC Tail Substation; LOT 2A: EPC for the HVDC subsea and underground cable system, and for the HVAC underground cable system in Wales (Bodelwyddan); LOT 2B: EPC for the supply and installation of HVAC cable system in Ireland (Dublin). The contract model for the lots will be amended FIDIC Conditions of Contract for EPC/Turnkey Projects (Silver Book). MaresConnect has conducted Preliminary Market Engagement prior to publication of this Contract Notice and encourages further collaboration between OEMs and Construction Contractors to establish bidding arrangements in time for the next step of the Procurement Process (notably the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire).

description: The Department of National Defence (DND), on behalf of the Canadian Forces School of Search and Rescue (CFSSAR), requires hotel accommodation services in Eloy, Arizona, to support parachute training activities from 23 November to 5 December 2026 and 27 March to 24 April 2027. Accommodation must include single and double occupancy rooms, Wi-Fi, housekeeping services, laundry facilities, on-site parking, fitness facilities, breakfast service, and access to cooking facilities. Rooms must be non-smoking and include private washrooms, air conditioning, refrigerators, televisions, and workstations. During the Para Phase (March-April 2027), accommodation providers must be able to ensure complete separation between CFSSAR staff and students through separate buildings or controlled, physically separated areas. Further details are contained within the solicitation documents.

title: Medicaid Data Analysis for Bacterial Respiratory Pathogens and Information Systems
description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) awarded a sole source contract with MATHEMATICA INC., 1100 1ST ST NE FL 12, WASHINGTON, DC. 20002 This notice is provided in accordance with RFO FAR 8.401 & GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) . Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases, Division of Bacterial Diseases (DBD) requires support Services with the contractor listed above. The requested contractor Mathematica qualified as �innovator status� vendor for data analysis by Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS). Mathematica also has demonstrated experience and specialized staff with unique access and analytical capabilities for Medicaid data sets which captures the largest segment of US healthcare data, including births. The contractor shall perform analyses across four technical dimensions defined in the Statement of Work: (1) validating infant GBS case counts using TAF OT claims and evaluating a fourth case definition tied to maternal Medicaid IDs; (2) developing and refining a probabilistic mother-infant linkage algorithm using the Medicaid Case Number and supplementary variables; (3) estimating maternal vaccination coverage (COVID-19, influenza, Tdap, and prospectively RSV) accounting for bundled payment code effects; and (4) applying methods to reduce gestational age missingness using prenatal claims data. These tasks require continuity with linkage algorithms and case-definition logic Mathematica has already built and validated under prior CDC task orders. The authority permitting other than full and open competition is Title III of the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act of 1949 (41 U.S.C. 251, et seq.); Title 40 U.S.C. 501, Services for Executive Agencies, as implemented at FAR 8.401 and GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1) "Only one source is capable of providing the products, services, or solution required at the level of quality required because the products, services, or solutions are unique or highly specialized." Through its prior contracts, Mathematica has already built key parts of this analysis�including updating the medical codes used to identify cases, working to link mother and infant records more completely, and adjusting for how individual states handle Medicaid enrollment for newborns. This steady, hands-on progress means Mathematica starts this next phase of work already ahead, with the knowledge and tools in place that a new contractor would not have. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation to Robin C. Meyer, Contract Specialist, at rcm2@cdc.gov, which shall be considered by the agency. The deadline for submissions is Ocotber 31, 2026 at 4:30PM EST. The Government will review any/all information submitted to determine if other responsible sources exist that could provide this requirement. Information received in response to this announcement will be used solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement.

title: Architect & Engineering Services, Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award (A&E) Contracts needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs required by Federal Prison Industries (FPI)
description: The Federal Prison Industries (FPI) intends to solicit and award a competitively negotiated Architect and Engineer (A&E) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Contract needed for new construction, renovation, alteration and repairs. The Architect and Engineer (A&E) shall furnish professional architectural, engineering, and related technical services, as specified herein, to the United States Government, Department of Justice, Federal Prison Industries (FPI). The resulting contracts will consist of a one?year base period and will include options for four additional one?year periods. All work performed under this contract shall pertain to projects located at FPI facilities within the contiguous United States. Pursuant to the terms of this contract, the A&E may be required to perform services under the following major categories, including other closely related services as necessary: � Review design and construction documents prepared by other A&E firms or by FPI personnel. � Prepare, develop, and produce design and construction documents for new facility construction, facility additions, and renovation or modernization of existing facilities. � Develop detailed and accurate cost estimates for construction activities, renovations, contract modifications, and claims. � Conduct Value Engineering (V/E) analyses and perform additional cost evaluation studies, as required. � Develop, maintain, and update project schedules and construction schedules. � Provide assistance in preventing, mitigating, and resolving disputes or claims arising from design or construction activities. � Furnish comprehensive architectural and engineering services encompassing all disciplines necessary to ensure the successful execution and completion of assigned projects. � Provide, as required, studies; design development; construction documents; technical specifications; support during bid negotiation; construction administration; and project closeout services. � Develop procedures, prepare construction documents and work statements, support master planning efforts, conduct regulatory compliance evaluations, and assist in the preparation of design?build documentation. � Prepare construction specifications that uphold the principles of full and open competition. � Comply with all general requirements applicable to task orders issued under this contract. In accordance with the Brooks Architect-Engineer Act, award(s) shall be made to the successful firm(s) based on demonstrated competence and qualifications to perform the services at fair and reasonable prices. Prior to this solicitation issuance, technical evaluations were conducted. This solicitation was then issued to the most highly rated firm(s). Therefore, in response to the solicitation, consideration for a contract award will be based solely upon the hourly rates, overhead and profit that are proposed and found to be fair and reasonable. Offerors are advised that award maybe made without discussions. Therefore, the initial proposal should provide sufficient information to recommend award without discussions and should reflect the offeror�s ability to perform at a reasonable price.

Solicitation Number: N6833526Q1133 Point of Contact and Questions The Point of Contact (POC) for this solicitation is: Eric Glawson, eric.j.glawson.civ@us.navy.mil and Kelli Ryan, kelli.l.ryan3.civ@us.navy.mil. title: Leather Sheepskin Hair Type
description: Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support (DLATS), Clothing & Textiles (C&T) Directorate, is conducting research to determine industry capabilities for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This is a Sources Sought only and not a solicitation for proposals. This announcement is considered Market Research in accordance with FAR 10. DLA is the Defense Department�s principal buyer of multiple items within the Clothing & Textile industry that uses Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. Numerous item specifications utilize Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type as a component in a wide variety of items purchased by DLA Troop Support, such as AR/PD 12-01 with Change 8 Amendment 1 and AR/PD 17-06 with Amendment 3, for Helmet Retention Systems. The primary purpose of this announcement is to identify potential sources with domestic manufacturing capabilities of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. This announcement also seeks to determine the availability of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type production capacity, limitations and challenges. Domestic sources using Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type with domestic manufacturing capabilities are required in accordance with DFARS 252.225-7002-2(c) Preference for Certain Domestic Commodities (DEC 2017) All potential sources will be U.S. based. Additional market research may be conducted prior to posting any solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this Sources Sought, nor will the Government compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing the information provided to the Government. This Source Sought does not constitute a commitment from the Government and any information provided in response to this Sources Sought will be used for informational purposes only. Any proprietary information submitted will be protected if appropriately marked. Vendor participation is not a promise for future business with the Government. The information for the below items is provided for informational purposes. It is highly recommended that vendors review the technical documents for items you can support then decide to request specifications. Vendors should use the following link to request item Specification: https://www.dla.mil/TroopSupport/ClothingandTextiles/SpecRequest.aspx Please use the contract opportunity notice ID �Sources Sought Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type� to obtain access. Fill in the request for the Technical Package requirements needed and under Special Instructions annotate �URGENT � MARKET RESEARCH � EXPEDITE.� The applicable North American Industrial Classification System Code (NAICS) is 315990 Apparel Accessories and Other Apparel Manufacturing. Small business size standards matched to industry NAICS codes are published by the Small Business Administration and are available at http://www.sba.gov/content/table-small-business-size-standards. Contractors must be registered with the Central Contractor Registration (CCR) at System for Award Management (SAM) http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for an award. Representations and certifications must also be on record. Submission requirements: Responses to this Sources Sought must be sent to Ryan Reynolds Contract Specialist, via email at Ryan.Reynolds@dla.mil and to Michelle Falkowski, Contracting Officer, via email at Michelle.Falkowski@dla.mil by the response date in this notice and should include company name, CAGE code, company size/profile, any other supportive information and answers to the below questions for each item for which you are potentially interested in supplying/supporting. 1. What is the absolute minimum quantity required for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 2. What is your monthly minimum and maximum production capacity? 3. What is your current and maximum production rate of yards per week? 4. What is the minimum monthly production quantity required to be economically producible? 5. What is your available operating capacity at present? 6. What is the availability of the local labor pool? 7. Provide your Production Lead Time (PLT) for Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type. 8. Are there any issues with the availability of raw materials? 9. Please provide a summary of your current supply situation in terms of raw materials including major components, critical materials, lead-time issues, and suppliers. 10. Are you a supplier, distributor, contractor, or other of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type? 11. What is the country of origin of Leather, Sheepskin, Hair Type from your company? 12. In what country is your CAGE/NCAGE associated? Any information provided is voluntary.

title: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille
description: Majoitus-, ravintola- ja ryhmätilapalvelut Reumaliiton järjestämille Arkea tukeville -kursseille Hankinnan kohteena on Suomen Reumaliitto ry:n järjestämien Arkea tukevien -kurssien majoitus-, ruokailu- ja ryhmätilapalvelut. Hankinta koskee vuosina 2027 ja 2028 järjestettäviä kursseja. Lisäksi on mahdollisuus kahteen (2) optiovuoteen. Tarjouksia pyydetään kuudelta alueelta: Keski-Suomi, Pirkanmaa, Pohjois-Pohjanmaa, Pohjois-Savo, Päijät-Häme ja Helsinki-Uusimaa. Kursseja järjestetään vuosittain kahdeksan (8) valtakunnallisesti eri paikkakunnilla tilaajan määrittämällä tavalla. Kurssit ovat kestoltaan kahdesta vuorokaudesta (perjantaista - sunnuntaihin) neljään vuorokauteen (maanantaista -perjantaihin). Kursseilla on 16 -18 henkilöä. Kurssit on tarkoitettu aikuisille henkilöille, joilla on reuma tai muu tuki- ja liikuntaelinsairaus. Kurssipaikan majoitus-, ryhmä- ja ravintolatilojen tulee olla esteettömiä, jotta liikuntarajoitteiset henkilöt pystyvät toimimaan niissä. Invahuoneita tulee olla kahdesta kolmeen (2–3) kappaletta. Kurssipaikalle tulee voida saapua ja poistua julkisilla yhteyksillä, joiden pysäkki tai asema on enintään 500 metrin päässä kurssipaikasta (tai tarjoajan on mahdollista järjestää kuljetus kauempana olevalta pysäkiltä tai asemalta). Kaksi kursseista on luontopainotteisia, joten pihapiiristä tai lähiympäristöstä tulee löytyä helposti saavutettavia ja esteettömiä luontoreittejä. Kurssit järjestetään Sosiaali- ja terveysjärjestöjen avustuskeskuksen (STEA) myöntämällä valtionavustuksella. Hankittavan palvelun laajuus ja määrä perustuvat tulevan valtionavustuksen suuruuteen. Vuodelle 2027 myönnettävä valtionavustuksen määrä vahvistuu alkuvuodesta 2027. Hankinnan kohde ja sitä koskevat vaatimukset kuvataan tarkemmin liitteissä.,

Yhtiö hakee nyt seuraavalle hallihankkeelle edullista ja laadukasta hallivalmistajaa, joka toimii samalla hankkeen pääurakoijana. Pääurakoijan vastuulle kuuluu myös kohteen rakennesuunnittelu. Hankkeen tekniset ratkaisut pyritään tekemään siten, että lopputuloksena valmistuu laadukasta, mutta mahdollisimman kustannustehokasta toimintatilaa vuokralaisena toimiville teollisuusyrityksille. Pääsuunnittelun on toteuttanut Arkkitehtitoimisto Paloranta Oy, LVISA-suunnittelusta vastaa Ratech Oy. Kannuksen Raonhaan teollisuusalueelle suunniteltu noin 1000 m2 teollisuushalli toteutetaan kahdessa osassa. Tässä tarjouspyynnössä pyydetään tarjoamaan nyt rakennettavan neljän lohkon kokonaisuuden kokonaishinta, sekä mahdollisten lisätöiden tuntihinta. Ensimmäiset neljä lohkoa rakennetaan piirustusten mukaisesti ensin, loput kaksi lohkoa laajennetaan heti, kun rakennettavat tilat on saatu täytettyä vuokralaisilla. Rakentaminen on tarkoitus aloittaa välittömästi, pohjatyöt pyritään saamaan valmiiksi ennen talvea, hallin pystytys ja varustelu talven aikana, käyttöönotto mahdollisimman nopeasti keväällä 2027. Laajennuksen rakentamisen aikataulua ei ole määritelty, mutta rakentaminen pyritään toteuttamaan saman pääurakoitsijan kanssa. Laajennuksen toteutuksessa käytetään tämän tarjouskilpailun hintaa, joka sidotaan kuitenkin laajennuksen osalta yleiseen kustannusindeksiin. Laajennuksen toteutuksesta laaditaan tulevaisuudessa oma sopimus ja aikataulu. Hankkeen käytännön toteutus on kuvattu Urakkaohjelmassa. Salassapito ja muut hankintaa koskevat seikat YSE 1998 mukaisesti. Tarjouksen vähimmäisvaatimukset, hylkäämisperusteet ja pisteytys on kuvattu omassa dokumentissaan.,

title: Industry Day: A Government-Industry Exchange on Construction Contracting - An Invitation for Industry Partners to Collaborate with the United States Space Force Operational Contracting Enterprise
description: Industry teammates, the Senior Contracting Official (SCO) for Operational and Enterprise Space Contracting invites you to a pivotal event discussing the future of construction in the U.S. Space Force. We are creating a forum to hear industry concerns and clarify the purpose of these new authorities to move faster, not to limit competition or replace valuable tools like Multiple Award Construction Contracts (MACCs). We have been granted new, flexible authorities for construction contracting, including Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a, and we want to partner with you to redefine how we build for the future. Join Us To: Hear directly from the SCO on the commitment to a fair, transparent, and collaborative construction process. Understand the New Authorities - A clear breakdown of what Construction OTAs are (and what they aren't), the 2808a authority, and how these tools fit into the broader acquisition landscape. Teach Us - This is an opportunity for industry to educate the government on commercial construction best practices and innovative methods to go from concept to capability � faster. Event Details: Date: 14 September 2026 Time: 0900-1200 (General Session); 1300-1400 (One on One Sessions) Location: Innovation Hub, 2424 Garden of the Gods Rd, Colorado Springs, CO (Will also be presented on Microsoft Teams) Who Should Attend? This event is for members of the construction industry, specifically general contractors, to come together to discuss, the Department of the Air Force (USAF & USSF) contracting processes including the new authorities and how we can work better with industry partners to achieve a more efficient means of awarding projects. Limited to two personnel per company. Registration Form: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/w3yV4dh0zp

title: Serbia – Development consultancy services – Study on the Availability, Quality and EU Compliance of TEN-T Rest Areas, Safe and Secure Truck Parking Areas in the Western Balkans
description: The Permanent Secretariat of the Transport Community aims to conclude a service contract for preparation of the Study whose primary aim is to review the transposition of the TEN-T Regulation 1679/2024 in the Western Balkans region and to assess the current availability, quality, and compliance with the relevant EU legislation regarding the rest areas (RAs) and safe and secure parking areas (SSTPAs) along the Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) in the Western Balkans. The Study will deliver an inventory of RAs and SSTPAs along the TEN-T network (including border crossing points) in the Western Balkans populating TODIS (Transport Observatory Database/Information System) with these data, assessing their compliance with EU safety, security, and service standards. It will identify critical gaps, evaluate future demand, and provide policy, technical and investment recommendations for infrastructure upgrades. Furthermore, it will outline key findings and an action plan for implementation, supporting alignment with TEN-T requirements and enhancing road transport efficiency and safety. This Study could be helpful in situation that some of Western Balkans Regional Partners do not have defined locations and reserved spaces for RAs and SSTPAs within their spatial planning documentation. This Study will also enhance regulatory alignment with EU policies and practices. Specific tasks, deliverables, and requirements will be detailed and described in the Tender Specifications.

title: SOFTWARE LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: CorrelateIQ - Correlation-Based System Intelligence
description: CorrelateIQ reveals hidden relationships among many data streams at once, catching hidden patterns, early warning signs and operating shifts that single-variable monitoring overlooks. Built on analysis techniques from high-energy physics, this software from Los Alamos National Laboratory turns existing sensor and process data into practical insight that helps organizations prevent failures, protect quality and reduce downtime. Because the method makes no assumptions about where the data comes from, it applies to a wide range of numeric data, from manufacturing sensors and equipment logs to financial records, market data and scientific measurements. Overview Factories, laboratories, infrastructure networks, financial and real-estate markets now produce huge volumes of linked data from sensors, equipment logs and transactions. Most analytics tools, however, judge each variable separately or depend on fixed thresholds that trigger an alert only after a single reading crosses a limit. These methods have trouble spotting effects that arise from subtle interactions among many variables, such as gradual equipment wear, a drifting manufacturing process or a market entering a new phase. As a result, organizations often miss the earliest warning signals, react to failures only after they happen and leave much of the value in their data untapped. Teams in every data-reach fields need a practical way of understanding how an entire system behaves as a whole, not merely how each part performs alone. Key Benefits Spots early warning signs before small problems become costly failures Uncovers the hidden factors that drive outcomes such as quality, risk or price Reveals relationships across many data sources that conventional tools miss Identifies which combinations of variables matter most Gets more value from data organizations already collect Works across industries and data types, from factory sensors to financial records Condenses complex, high-volume data into clear, compact indicators Complements existing monitoring, machine learning and digital twin systems Core Capabilities At its core, CorrelateIQ: Correlation-Based System Intelligence measures collective behavior. Users choose the variables or signals of interest, and the software calculates higher-order correlations that capture how those inputs change together rather than separately. The framework accepts mixed data types, including time-series records, sensor readings, transactional data and scientific measurements. It condenses them into compact representations of overall system behavior. Because the software reduces many interacting variables to a smaller set of meaningful indicators, complex environments become easier to read, compare and act upon. CorrelateIQ also goes beyond a single snapshot. It tracks how correlation patterns change over time, so users can see shifts in operating state, new anomalies and transitions from one regime to another. Its outputs can act as an analytics or feature-generation layer that feeds existing monitoring, control or machine learning systems. It can run in real-time monitoring pipelines or offline analytics platforms. Planned improvements include automated selection and ranking of the most useful correlations, adaptive correlation building and closer integration with predictive maintenance and digital twin workflows. Use Cases & Market Applications Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing (process monitoring, quality control) Industrial operations and energy (predictive maintenance, equipment health) Infrastructure (structural health monitoring, multisensor networks) Industrial software and digital twins (system modeling, feature generation) Finance and real estate (market shift detection, risk analysis) Scientific research (physics data analysis, complex systems studies) Healthcare, transportation and cybersecurity (anomaly detection, early warning) Supply chains and climate monitoring (leading indicators, change detection) LA-UR-26-29216 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: Performance Measurement for the Medicare Advantage Program
description: This posting provides notice that the Limited Sources Justification (LSJ) for the Performance Measurement for the Medicare Advantage Program procurement is being posted pursuant to GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(3)(i), which requires the ordering activity to publish a notice and post the justification within 14 days after placing an order exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold that is supported by an LSJ. Section 1859(f)(5) of the Social Security Act (�the Act�) requires that organizations offering specialized Medicare Advantage (MA) plans for special needs individuals have in place an evidenced-based model of care (MOC) with appropriate networks of providers and specialists. In addition, Section 1859(f)(7) of the Act requires that a Medicare Advantage Organization (MAO) offering a specialized MA plan for special needs individuals (i.e., special needs plan, or SNP) be approved by the National Committee for Quality Assurance (NCQA) based on standards established by the Secretary. This requirement is implemented at 42 CFR ��422.101(f) and 422.152(g) and requires MAOs offering SNPs to have NCQA review and approve the required MOC each SNP submits to CMS on a regular basis. The Healthcare Effectiveness Data and Information Set (HEDIS�) is a widely used set of health plan performance measures employed by both private and public health care purchasers to promote accountability and to assess the quality of care provided by managed care organizations. NCQA owns the proprietary rights to HEDIS� and the system that collects HEDIS� data. It is the only organization authorized to add quality measurements to HEDIS� and to provide technical assistance to commercial and Medicare health plans and auditors in the use of these measurements. Section 1853(o)(6)(A) of the Act states that the Secretary may require reporting of data under section 1852(e) for, and apply under this subsection, quality measures at the plan level for specialized MA plans for special needs individuals instead of at the contract level. The purpose of this task order is to support CMS in the evaluation and approval of each SNP�s model of care (MOC). As noted above, Section 1859(f)(7) of the Act and 42 CFR ��422.4(a)(1)(iv), 422.101(f), and 422.152(g) require that each MAO offering a SNP must submit a MOC to be approved by NCQA. Please see the Attachments section of this notice for a complete copy of the approved LSJ. Note - This is NOT an active procurement opportunity but is instead a required posting of an approved LSJ subsequent to task order award.

title: Replacement of Facade Lights
description: This is the U.S. Embassy Riga Pre-Solicitation Notice only. Contractors are required to read the requirements below. No responses are requested by this notice. The U.S. Embassy Riga issues this notice with the intent of giving an opportunity to all interested parties to appropriately prepare for the anticipated Request for quotes (RFQ). This is not a request for proposal; this is for pre-solicitation/informational purposes only. No award will be made based on responses received to this notice. The requirement is to furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision necessary to remove the existing exterior facade lighting fixtures and install new RGBW LED facade lighting fixtures at the U.S. Embassy Riga, Latvia. U.S. Embassy Riga is currently illuminated by iGuzzini Linealuce B752 facade light fixtures. The Department seeks to replace these fixtures with individually addressable RGBW LED fixtures. To ensure rapid installation, ongoing maintenance, and ready access to materials and skilled labor, it is necessary to procure locally. U.S.-based fabricators are not positioned to service installations in Latvia, and sourcing materials or technical support from the United States would result in unacceptable delays and increased costs. Local procurement will ensure the Embassy can complete the work within the required timeframe and minimize future operational disruptions.

title: DA10--DB Protect Software and Maintenance Bridge (VA-26-00089068)(New Work)
description: This requirement was for a firm-fixed price delivery order (DO) issued under National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Solution for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V Government wide Acquisition Contract (GWAC) contract NNG15SD20B with Cynergy Professional Systems LLC (Cynergy) to provide brand name TrustWave Holdings Inc. (TrustWave) DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. Cynergy is a Small Business Administration Certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) that is an authorized reseller for brand name TrustWave DbProtect term software licenses with maintenance and technical support. TrustWave DbProtect licensing and support are proprietary and can only be procured directly from an authorized TrustWave provider. Because the database security environment relies on TrustWave s unique architecture, integrations, and maintenance protocols, any attempt to obtain licensing or support through an alternate source would result in delays, incompatibility risks, and unacceptable gaps in security coverage. Cynergy is the current provider and will ensure uninterrupted protection of mission critical systems. Without the required TrustWave DbProtect licensing, the VA would be unable to perform essential database vulnerability scans, leaving critical systems unmonitored. This inability to assess and identify security risks would place the VA s data and infrastructure under undue and unacceptable risk. No other brand name database vulnerability scanning platform is interoperable with VA s existing TrustWave DbProtect infrastructure, database structures, and software application programming interfaces due to the proprietary constraints of the TrustWave infrastructure currently implemented within VA. Specifically, due to the proprietary constraints within the software source code, any other Original Equipment Manufacturer s (OEM) solution would not be able to communicate with the VA s existing TrustWave software licenses to provide the necessary database scanning and database vulnerability data collection, as well as critical updates, patches, updates to TrustWave DbProtect's Shatter Knowledge database, and bug fixes needed to ensure the infrastructure continues to function as intended.

title: Technical Support for Payment Systems and Rates
description: This posting provides notice that the limited-sources justification (LSJ) for the Technical Support for Payment Systems and Rates procurement is being posted pursuant to GSAR 538.7104-3(b)(3)(i), which requires the ordering activity to publish a notice and post the justification within 14 days after placing an order exceeding the simplified acquisition threshold that is supported by an LSJ. The agency requires the continuation of highly specialized ratesetting and related enterprise architecture activities that have been developed, refined, and maintained by Acumen since 2010. Acumen is the only responsible source capable of providing the required services at the level of quality and technical sophistication necessary to meet agency needs at this time. With more than a decade of continuous performance, Acumen has developed substantial institutional knowledge, proprietary analytical tools, and refinements to ratesetting models that are not replicated elsewhere in the market. These capabilities are currently inseparable from the agency's operational workflows and are essential for accurate, timely data production and the execution of rulemaking schedules. The current period aligns with critical milestones in the SAS Conversion and broader enterprise architecture modernization efforts, and introducing a new vendor at this stage would create significant operational and programmatic risk. Transitioning midstream would require reconstruction and relearning of proprietary methodologies, duplication of already-funded development, and revalidation of highly technical processes�all of which would result in unacceptable delays and substantial additional costs. Because the required work is deeply integrated with ongoing modernization activities and the SAS Conversion effort, switching vendors at this time would require extensive re-familiarization, redevelopment of analytical baselines, and re-establishment of complex data linkages. Such a transition would reduce efficiency, waste previously obligated funds, and delay key milestones associated with data validation and model conversion. While the continued Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) task order independently qualifies as a logical follow-on under FAR 8.405-6, the broader justification for continuity with Acumen further reflects the sole-source considerations described above. This acquisition also qualifies as a logical follow-on to the original Federal Supply Schedule order as it was awarded competitively using the General Services Administration (GSA)�s Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) SIN 541611. Continuing the work with Acumen is essential to preserving technical and operational continuity across interconnected workstreams that cannot be separated or re-sequenced without jeopardizing mission-critical deliverables. The ratesetting models, data production schedules, and enterprise architecture components under this contract directly support multiple regulatory and rulemaking timelines. Interrupting performance or onboarding a new vendor would compromise the sequencing and validation of these processes, introducing significant risk to statutory and policy deadlines. A short-term logical follow-on ensures continuity of operations, preserves the value of prior investments, and allows adequate time for full and open competition in 2028. It also gives the agency sufficient runway to develop updated metrics, engage with industry, build internal subject-matter expertise, and design a more targeted and cost-effective competitive strategy. Continuing the work with Acumen is therefore the most efficient and economical approach, and it squarely satisfies the FAR requirement for a logical follow-on acquisition. Please see the Attachments section of this notice for a complete copy of the approved LSJ. Note - This is NOT an active procurement opportunity but is instead a required posting of an approved LSJ subsequent to task order award.

title: GSA A/E SHORT SELECTION PROCESS FOR CONUS/OCONUS
description: Description The purpose of this announcement is to request new Architect / Engineer (A/E) qualification information for the General Services Administration / Public Buildings Service (GSA/PBS) A/E short selection for Continental United States (CONUS) and Outside Continental United States (OCONUS). WHAT IS THE SHORT SELECTION PROCESS? The short selection process utilizes the procedures set forth in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Subsection 36.202-4 for Architect/Engineer (A/E) projects with an estimated total fee less than the simplified acquisition threshold (currently $350,000; see RFO FAR Part 2.101). The A/E's professional qualifications, the firm's geographic proximity, knowledge of the local area as identified on the A/E's SF330, and supplemental information will be used for the first preliminary screening of firms. For each proposed project, GSA will conduct discussions with at least three (3) firms to consider anticipated concepts and compare alternative methods for furnishing services. Additional information may be requested during discussions if necessary to facilitate the final ranking of firms (i.e.: past performance references, specialized experience, capacity, schedule, etc.). Upon conclusion of discussions, the top three firms will be ranked, and a price proposal will be requested from the highest ranked firm. If a fair and reasonable price cannot be negotiated with the highest ranked firm, a request for a price proposal will be sent to the second ranked firm, and so on until an award can be made at a fair and reasonable price. All acquisitions utilizing the GSA A/E short selection list (database) shall be set-aside for small business concerns unless requirements cannot be met by a small business and the Contracting Officer (CO) obtains a proper waiver. WHAT IS THE SHORT SELECTION PROCESS USED FOR? GSA will use the short selection list to award A/E contracts, valued at less than the simplified acquisition threshold (currently $350,000) in CONUS/OCONUS (NOT Estimated Cost of Construction at Award (ECCA). The firm must have NAICS code 541310 - Architectural Services, with a small business size standard of $12.5 million and/or 541330 - Engineering Services, with a small business size standard of $25.5 million. The firm must clearly notate which states/territories they have active production offices and which states they are licensed by November 1, 2026. Most work will be executed for repair and alteration projects within existing Federal Buildings and U.S. Courthouses. The estimated cost of construction at award (ECCA) for a majority of the project requirements could range from, but are not limited to, above micro-purchase threshold for construction (currently $2,000) to annual prospectus threshold (currently $3.961M) or higher. Fees for design services cannot exceed 6% of the ECCA. For more information about the 6% fee limitation, see FAR 15.404-9(c)(4)(ii) (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and 41 U.S.C. 3905(b)(3). GSA manages a nationwide real estate portfolio of approximately 360 million rentable square feet, including preserving more than 500 historic properties nationwide. A/E Disciplines and Expertise - A/E firms will need staff with licensed and/or specialized expertise. The following are typical disciplines and categories utilized for GSA projects. Firms do not need to have all of them, but should include the most relevant disciplines for their firm: Core Architectural and Engineering Disciplines Architecture and anterior architecture Mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, structural & civil engineering, and plumbing Historic architecture/preservation Specialized Expertise A qualified/licensed fire protection engineer (NCEES)* Security Space planning & workplace Cost estimating and scheduling Environmental services Building automation Scifs Modernization and Quality Control Building information modeling (BIM) Quality control review and report writing SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS To be considered for future Architect-Engineer (A/E) projects, your firm must submit a package demonstrating the applicability and comparability of its portfolio to the types of services outlined above. description: Dear DoC Contractors, The Department of Commerce (DoC) is implementing a financial systems modernization project that will result in use of the Invoice Processing Platform (IPP) for the submittal and payment of invoices.* Please note that, beginning October 2026 the bureaus and offices** listed below will transition to use of IPP: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) International Trade Administration (ITA) Minority Business Development Agency (MBDA) National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) National Technical Information Service (NTIS) Office of Inspector General (OIG) Office of the Secretary (OS) IPP is a secure, Web-based electronic invoicing system provided to federal agencies and their vendors at no charge, by the U.S. Department of the Treasury�s Bureau of the Fiscal Service. By using IPP, vendors can receive electronic Purchase Orders (POs) and send electronic invoices, either through file exchange or by pulling data for invoices directly from POs. IPP also provides online access to invoice status and payment information, including offsets. Prior to transition to use of IPP the clause entitled Invoice Processing Platform-Alternate I (Dec 2022) shall apply to all existing contract actions for these bureaus/offices. After transition to IPP the clause entitled Invoice Processing Platform (Dec 2022) shall apply to all contract actions for these bureaus/offices. The full text of these clauses is attached here for reference. In anticipation of these bureaus/offices transition to IPP please review the information available at https://www.ipp.gov/knowledge-center/vendors/getting-started. If not already enrolled, the Contractor Government Business Point of Contact (as listed in SAM) will receive enrollment instructions via email within three to five business days of the addition of the contract award to IPP, which is anticipated to occur in the October 2026 timeframe. Contractor assistance with enrollment can be obtained by contacting the IPP Production Helpdesk via email: IPPCustomerSupport@fiscal.treasury.gov or phone (866) 973-3131. Please distribute this information broadly to personnel within your company who may be affected by the transition and if you have questions regarding the implementation of IPP for these bureaus/offices please contact the Shared Services Procurement Office at SharedServicesProcurement@doc.gov. Sincerely, Shared Services Procurement Office www.commerce.gov/oam/? *NOTE 1: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Census Bureau, the Economic Development Administration (EDA), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) have already transitioned to use of IPP. **NOTE 2: In addition to the bureaus/offices listed above, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the First Responder Network Authority (FirstNet) will also transition to use of IPP in October 2026. Please contact your NIST and FirstNet points of contact with any questions specific to use of IPP for contracts your firm may hold with NIST or FirstNet.
